exposure: etiology of DAT positivity (ABO-incompatibility, Rh incompatibility, minor blood group incompatibility, other RBC-related antibodies, unspecified etiology)
outcome: development of hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN)
need for therapeutic interventions (phototherapy, exchange transfusion, intravenous immunoglobulin)
cohort: Neonates born at a tertiary academic hospital between January 2011 and December 2020, specifically 176 neonates with a positive DAT result and a comparison group of DAT-negative neonates.
finding: ABO incompatibility was the most common cause for neonatal DAT positivity and HDN, with DAT-positive neonates exhibiting higher initial bilirubin levels, lower hemoglobin levels, and a significantly greater need for therapeutic interventions compared to DAT-negative neonates.
